page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 24 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI for vectorized execution and inference workloads, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration via AES. The instance is paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations, and zero GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned.

Benchmark results show balanced single-thread capability counterbalanced by lower multi-core scaling. The instance logged a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1572.39, both placing within the middle 50% category. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (4147.67) and Geekbench multi-core (2855.0) place in the bottom 25% bracket. Memory throughput evaluates at 28.26 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 24.11 GB/sec for writes, earning an average PassMark memory score of 2070.5. Compression benchmarks follow a similar profile, yielding average throughput in single-threaded gzip (26.8 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (10.09 GB/sec), but falling into the bottom 10% on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (18.77 GB/sec).

Application performance reflects the constraints of its 4-vCPU density. Static web serving throughput reaches 4.11 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET throughput measures 4.1 million operations per second, both residing in the lower 25th percentile. On AI inference tests with a small 135M model, prompt evaluation hit 267.33 tokens per second (bottom 25%), while generation throughput achieved 74.92 tokens per second (middle 50%). With no bundled local disks or hardware accelerators, this configuration serves best as an entry-tier compute-focused node for moderate single-threaded services, lightweight build automation, compilation jobs, or containerized microservices that benefit from high baseline clock speeds and AVX-512 support without requiring massive parallel throughput.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized instance delivering 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. Built on 2 physical cores with hyper-threading, it includes 24 MB of L3 cache alongside AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI instruction sets. The server includes no bundled local storage or GPUs. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates mid-tier single-core CPU execution, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1309.0 and steady single-threaded compression speeds. Conversely, overall multi-core and application scaling fall in the bottom quartile, illustrated by a multi-core Geekbench score of 2855.0 and Redis throughput of 4.1 million operations per second. With an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, c2-standard-4 is suited for moderately threaded computational tasks, Clang build agents, web backends, and lightweight inference deployments requiring dedicated processing frequency without extensive parallel resource demands.
